A.explanation: RS does not show alternating maxima and minima because the path difference from P and Q is zero everywhere on RS, so XY alone shows a pattern.

B.explanation: Every point on RS is equidistant from P and Q, giving constant constructive interference and no fringe pattern.

C.explanation: Along XY the path difference $PS - QS$ grows from zero at S, producing successive constructive and destructive interference, i.e. a fringe pattern.

D.explanation: A varying path difference occurs along XY, so an interference pattern of maxima and minima is observed there.

hints: Notice that RS is the perpendicular bisector of PQ, so compare the distances from P and from Q to any point on RS.
Recall that the type of interference depends on path difference, with $0$ or $n\lambda$ giving constructive and $(n+1/2)\lambda$ giving destructive interference.
Check how the path difference changes when moving away from S along XY compared with moving along RS, where RS is much longer than PQ.
walkthrough: Identify the sources: P and Q are coherent, so the observed intensity depends on the path difference $\Delta = |d_P - d_Q|$ at each observation point.
Consider line RS: it is half-way between P and Q and perpendicular to PQ, so by symmetry every point on RS is equidistant from P and Q.
Therefore along RS $\Delta = 0$ everywhere, giving continuous constructive interference with no alternation between maxima and minima.
Consider line XY: at S the distances are equal so $\Delta = 0$, but moving toward X or toward Y makes one source nearer than the other, so $\Delta$ increases steadily.
As $\Delta$ increases through $0, \lambda/2, \lambda, 3\lambda/2$ and so on, the interference alternates between constructive and destructive, forming a fringe pattern.
Hence a varying interference pattern is seen along XY only. This is option C
